You don’t need a huge following to get discovered. Algorithms care more about whether your content is relevant than how many followers you have.

Social media discoverability is how easily new people can find your brand’s account and content on social platforms. That includes showing up when someone searches for a topic, or appearing in their feed because an algorithm thinks they’ll be interested.

Why does social media discoverability matter?

Social media discoverability matters because it helps your content reach people who don’t follow you yet. The easier your content is to find, the more chances you have to get in front of new audiences without paying for their attention.
Here’s why discoverability is more important than ever:
People are using social media as a search engine
66% of U.S. consumers now use social media as a search tool, according to a 2025 eMarketer study.
Maybe they’re checking YouTube to see if a viral air fryer is worth the hype. Or searching TikTok for haircare tips.
If your content isn’t built to be found, you’re missing those searches entirely.
Not too long ago, your social feed was made up of accounts you chose to follow. Now, most social media algorithms bubble up content from accounts you’ve never heard of.

“The algorithm works differently now, suggesting content to users based on their interests,” says Monica Panait, Chief Marketing Officer of Brizy. “I’ve noticed that even a small account can reach hundreds of thousands of people if users find it interesting and useful.”
That’s the power of discoverability: When a platform understands your content, it can connect you with new audiences.
You reach people without paying for every impression
Discoverable content helps your team reach new people without putting a budget behind every post. That gives you another way to grow your audience organically, without depending on paid campaigns.
Your content can keep working for longer
Most posts fade from the feed within a day or two. But a post that shows up in search can keep pulling in new viewers for weeks (or even months) after it goes live.
That’s especially true for content people look up again and again, like tutorials, explainers, and product reviews.
How do people discover content on social media?

People discover social media content through in-app search, algorithm recommendations, hashtags and topics, Google results, and AI answers. Each offers a different way to reach new audiences, so it pays to understand how they work.

In-app search: This is the most direct route. Someone types a question or keyword into a platform’s search bar, like “best hiking shoes,” and the platform shows posts that match. If your content answers that question, it has a shot at showing up.

Algorithmic recommendations: Social algorithms recommend posts based on what people have liked, saved, and watched before, even from accounts they don’t follow. Think TikTok’s For You page or Instagram’s Explore tab.
Hashtags and topics: Hashtags help platforms categorize posts, while topics connect people with specific interests. Both can make it easier for your content to reach the right audience.

Google results: Google can surface content from Reddit threads, Facebook, YouTube, and LinkedIn in its search engine results. Instagram joined the club in 2025, letting search engines index posts from professional accounts.
AI answers: AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini can cite social media posts in their answers. Learn more in our guide to AI search optimization.
These discovery paths often overlap, so optimizing your content for one can help it get found in other places.
How do you improve social media discoverability?

You improve social media discoverability by making it easy for both people and algorithms to understand what your content is about. That involves using relevant keywords, adding on-screen text and captions to videos, and sticking to a few core topics.
Here’s how to put that into practice:
Optimize your profile handle, name, and bio
Use relevant keywords in your captions
Add on-screen text and captions to videos
Stick to a few core topics
1. Optimize your profile handle, name, and bio
Your profile does a lot of quiet work. It helps social platforms understand your account, and it helps new visitors decide if you’re worth a follow.
Handle: Keep it recognizable and consistent across social networks.
Profile name: Consider adding a keyword that describes what you do. On most platforms, your profile name is searchable, so “Maya the Vegan Baker” gives people more to go on than just “Maya.”
Bio: Describe what you do, and work in a few natural-sounding keywords. For example, a bakery could add “custom cakes” to its bio instead of relying on its business name alone.
2. Write captions with the keywords your audience searches
Think about what someone would type into the search bar to find a post like yours.
For example, if you’re sharing a video about caring for indoor plants, “how to care for a fiddle-leaf fig” is a more useful caption than “Plant parent problems.”
Once you have a keyword or two, put them near the start of your caption and write the rest naturally. Don’t overdo it, though. If it reads like a list of search terms, people will keep scrolling.
3. Add on-screen text and captions to video
Social media algorithms are getting smarter. Along with your caption, they can now pick up on-screen text and spoken audio to understand what your video is about.
Say your keyword out loud in the first few seconds. Since platforms can pick up on spoken words, saying the keyword out loud genuinely helps.
Add on-screen text that clearly describes the topic of the video, ideally near the beginning.
Turn on captions (or add your own) so the spoken words are readable too. Bonus: Captions are a win for accessibility.
Hashtags still have a place in your social media strategy, so long as you use them carefully.

For starters, pick hashtags that actually describe your post. A mix of one broad tag and a couple of niche ones usually works well. For example, a skincare brand might use #skincare (a broad hashtag), along with #sensitiveskin and #skincareroutine.
And skip trending hashtags that have nothing to do with your content. They might get you in front of more people, but not the right ones.
5. Stick to a few core topics

Choose a handful of topics that make sense for your brand, then post about them regularly. The idea is to give the algorithms consistent signals about what your content is about, so they can match it to the right users.

That doesn’t mean you have to post about the same thing every day. There’s still room to jump on a trend, or post something just for fun. Just make sure most of your content ties back to your core topics.

Engagement helps your content so beyond the bubble of your own audience. When people save, share, or comment on a post, it sends signals to the algorithm that others might find it interesting, too.
A few ways to encourage more engagement:
Create save-worthy content. Think checklists, how-tos, or tips people will want to reference later.
Ask better questions. “Thoughts?” doesn’t always inspire a response. A specific question (“Which would you try first?”) gives people an easy reason to comment.
Add clear CTAs: Even a small nudge like, “Save this for later,” can boost replies and shares.
And skip the engagement bait. People can usually tell when a post is fishing for engagement, and nobody likes being told to “comment YES” for no reason.
Collaborations are one of the fastest ways to reach new people. When you team up with another account, you get introduced to their followers (and they get introduced to yours).

Instagram makes this easy with Collab posts. You invite another account as a collaborator, and once they accept, the post shows up on both profiles. The likes, comments, and views all land on one shared post.
Just make sure the partnership makes sense for both audiences. Our influencer marketing guide covers how to find the right creators.
Cross-promotion helps too. If you’ve built an audience on Instagram, for example, you could point them toward your YouTube channel for longer videos.

How do you measure social media discoverability?

Measuring social media discoverability means looking at how many new people find your content and where they come from. Specifically, focus your attention on metrics that show non-follower activity. That’s how you’ll know you’re reaching new people.
Non-follower reach: The share of your reach that comes from people who don’t follow you. Instagram and TikTok both break this out in their native analytics.
Traffic sources: Several platforms show where views came from, such as search, recommendations, or your profile. A growing share from search is a great sign.
Profile visits: This shows how many new viewers peeked at your profile after watching your content.
Share of voice: How much of the conversation in your space mentions your brand compared to competitors.
Compare these metrics month over month. The goal is steady improvement over time.

The most common discoverability mistakes are judging success by follower count alone, posting without a clear focus, and stuffing captions with keywords. Most of them are easy to fix once you know what to look for.
Judging success by follower count alone

Follower count used to be the golden metric of social media success. More followers meant more people seeing your posts. But now that algorithms recommend content to people outside your audience, a big chunk of your audience could be complete strangers.

When your social content bounces between unrelated topics, the algorithm has a harder time figuring out who to show it to. It also makes it hard to build or grow an audience, since nobody knows what to expect.

Keywords help, but only up to a point. A caption crammed with search terms reads like spam, and people won’t stick around long enough to engage. Write for a person first, then make sure your main keyword shows up naturally.

Social media discoverability is how easily people can find your brand and content on social media platforms, even if they don’t already follow you. That includes showing up in search results and getting recommended by algorithms. Good discoverability helps you reach new audiences and grow your brand visibility without relying entirely on paid ads.
How do I make my social media content more discoverable?

Start by making your content easy for both people and platforms to understand. Add keywords to your profile, captions, and on-screen text, stick to a few core topics, and create posts people want to save and share. It works a lot like traditional SEO. The goal is to match your content to the words people actually search for.
How do social media algorithms decide who sees your posts?

Algorithms look at what each person has watched, liked, saved, and searched for, then recommend posts that match those interests. They also pay attention to how people react to your post. If early viewers save, share, or comment, the platform takes that as a sign to show it to more people. Each platform weighs these signals a little differently.
Do hashtags still help people discover your content?

Yes, but they work differently than they used to. These days, hashtags act more like labels that help platforms sort your content, so a few specific, relevant tags will do more than a long list of popular ones. Think of them as one piece of your social SEO strategy, along with your captions, profile, and on-screen text.
